is: Five slash commands the Engineer runs in the design session: release objectives, the queue, catch-up briefings, doc comments and retrospectives, each usable without the zaf instances.
conventions: each skill reads a 1.x project's `.claude/TEAMS.md` (or `.yaml`, `.toml`) when present, and otherwise detects what it needs and asks once
my-queue and catch-me-up are read-only; document edits doc comments only, never logic

fs.name: catch-me-up/
fs.role: /teams:catch-me-up: spoken briefing of where things stand, from the board, the release folder and VCS history

fs.name: document/
fs.role: /teams:document: doc comments on what changed, in each language's style and placement

fs.name: my-queue/
fs.role: /teams:my-queue: the Engineer's Ready, Incoming, Questions, Waiting and Optional tables from the board or a queue file and live PRs

fs.name: objectives/
fs.role: /teams:objectives: interviews the Engineer into a release's objectives.md, has a fresh teams:designer challenge it, records the signature; objectives-template.md is the file's skeleton

fs.name: retrospective/
fs.role: /teams:retrospective: Claude's own evidence-based retro over a time range, from commits, PRs and reviews

notes: the release instance checks each must in a signed objectives.md before it merges the version, so this skill feeds release.md
a release's retrospective belongs to the release instance (from `zaf report` and `zaf asklog`), not to /teams:retrospective
the 1.x skills /teams:prepare-pr, cleanup, critique and address-comments were retired in 2.0.0 into zaf verbs (`zaf slice pr`, `zaf slice merge`/`drop`, `zaf check`)
